newsitem.title: MALTA: Maltese man accused of selling bogus whisky.
newsitem.headline: Maltese man accused of selling bogus whisky.

text.p: A 28-year-old man was arraigned before a Maltese court on Monday accused of selling bogus whisky, vodka and gin.
The man sold hundreds of bottles containing vinegar instead of whisky and water instead of vodka and gin. He sold the bottles at below normal prices mostly to political clubs.
The sales took place in January, days after the government announced a 10 percent rise in the price of wines and spirits.
Newspapers said at the time that the bottles, bearing the labels of well-known brands of spirits, appeared to be sealed and did not indicate they had been tampered with.
One newspaper said this was the miracle of Cana in reverse. According to scripture Jesus Christ turned water into wine during a wedding party in the town of Cana.
